output.brief: The Android login drop is almost certainly caused by the vendor's edge rule update on 3 March, not by release 6.14. A new rule (AUTO-LIB-17) blocks requests from the app's networking library on the password-login path. It started at 10:41 UTC, about three minutes after the rule pack went live. It returns 403 to roughly 9,600 requests a day, and 92% of the blocked installs are existing, legitimate customers. The drop is identical on every app version, including old ones that were not updated. It is identical on every OS version, patched or not. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are unaffected, and the failures started at the rule time rather than at the 3 March 09:00 rollout start. Credential stuffing, the OS patch and the token-lifetime change don't fit the pattern. Rolling back 6.14 or reverting the password screen would not help. Raising bot sensitivity would block more customers. Excluding blocked attempts from the KPI would hide the real problem. Next step: ask Corvane to put the rules added on 3 March into log-only mode on the mobile password path, keeping rate limits, lockout and other rules on. Then confirm in telemetry that password success recovers to about 96%. Ask Corvane for a proper fix, and make vendor rule updates subject to testing. The call-volume link is plausible but not proven, since fee notices went out the same week.
